messages.subject: weird error message with Lavaan
parts:
Hi, Lavaan users:

I am trying to do latent change score analysis in Lavaan. 

I have two data points--T1 and T2. I cannot fix the error I got--still new to Lavaan. The error message was:

Error in tmp[cbind(REP$row[idx], REP$col[idx])] <- lavpartable$free[idx] : 
  NAs are not allowed in subscripted assignments

Here is my Lavaan syntax:

model<-"   # Latent variables
           F1 =~ 1*t1var1 + b*t1var2 +s*t1var3
           F2 =~ 1*t2var1 + b*t2var2 +s*t2var3 
          # intercept
           t1var1   ~ it1*1
           t2var1   ~ it1*1
           t1var2   ~ ib1*1
           t2var2   ~ ib1*1
           t1var3   ~ is1*1
           t2var3   ~ is1*1          
           # covariance
           F1~F2    
           # residual variance
           t1var1 ~ t2var1
           t1var2 ~ t2var2
           t1var3 ~ t2var3
           #latent means
           F1 ~0*1  # baseline
           F2 ~1    # difference compared with baseline
           "
 fit  <- cfa(model, data=data, ordered=c("t1var1", "t2var1","t1var2", "t2var2","t1var3", "t2var3"),
            std.lv=FALSE, meanstructure=TRUE, estimator = "WLSMV")

I checked. The variables' names are in standard format. No brackets or other nonstandard symbols.

Anyone has an idea??

Would appreciate any help.

Grace

messages.subject: Re: weird error message with Lavaan
parts:
I also noticed that your using ordered variables; therefore, you do not need to specify the intercepts (this may very well be the reason why you get the error using older versions of lavaan); remove them from the model; the same story with the residual variances, they are not needed (because they are a function of other model parameters); remove them from the model.

Yves.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: weird error message with Lavaan
parts: There is one typo for residuals. It should be "~~", not "~".

Same typo here:

           # covariance
           F1~F2    

Although for a latent change score, I think you need to regress time 2 on time 1

           F2 ~ F1    

and fix the residual for F2 to zero, then define a phantom construct for the F2 residual that represents the change score.

Also, you are imposing invariance constraints on the intercepts, but you are still estimating all intercepts and (implicitly, using the default) fixing the latent means to zero for identification.  So there can't be any latent change in the model as you have specified it -- both means are fixed to zero. 

Terry

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: weird error message with Lavaan
parts: one of my endogeneous variables is binary and therefore I declared it as 'ordered'. To estimate the indirect effects conditional on the moderator, I need to specify the intercept

That intercept was specified to condition effects on the mean (+/- 1 SD) of the moderator.  Is your binary endogenous variable the moderator (so the intercept is not necessarily the grand mean)?  Please share the details of your model (path diagram, lavaan syntax).
Is there another way to specify the indirect effects conditional on the moderator than suggested in Hallquist's code (e.g., that cirumvents specifying the intercept)?

You can just look at the descriptive statistics of your moderator to know the mean and SD.  Specifying that in the syntax directly may also shrink your SEs because the delta method will not be treating the conditioning data as uncertain estimates themselves.

FYI, Hallquist's syntax mistakenly omits the mean from the conditional effects for 1 SD +/- the mean.  It should be:

indirect.SDbelow := a1*b + a3*(write.mean - sqrt(write.var))*b
indirect.mean    := a1*b + a3* write.mean                   *b 
indirect.SDabove := a1*b + a3*(write.mean + sqrt(write.var))*b
